v4ApiEntries.name: cytoscape
v4ApiEntries.summary: Create a GPU-prototype cytoscape instance (issue #3486, pass 1): a columnar CPU-canonical model with a WebGPU render pipeline.

v4ApiEntries.name: cytoscape.toColumnarElements
v4ApiEntries.summary: Convert classic v3-style elements JSON into the columnar bulk-load form: typed-array columns with edge endpoints as node *indices*.

v4ApiEntries.name: cytoscape.serializeElements
v4ApiEntries.summary: Serialize elements (definition form or columnar form) into one transferable/fetchable ArrayBuffer.  `deserializeElements` (or passing the buffer straight to `options.elements`/`cy.add()`) reverses it.

v4ApiEntries.name: cytoscape.deserializeElements
v4ApiEntries.summary: Deserialize a `serializeElements` buffer (or a view over one) back into the columnar elements form.  Numeric columns are zero-copy views into the given buffer; a misaligned view is copied once to realign.

v4ApiEntries.name: cytoscape.CancelledError
v4ApiEntries.summary: Thrown (as a rejection) by a cancelled run: an async algorithm whose handle's `cancel()` was called, a layout's `promise()` after `layout.cancel()`, or either when `cy.destroy()` ran while the run was in flight.  `error.name` is `'CancelledError'`, so a `.catch` can tell a cancellation from a defect without importing the class.

v4ApiEntries.name: cytoscape.GpuUnfitError
v4ApiEntries.summary: Thrown when something does not fit the GPU device's limits.  Two places throw it:

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.ready
v4ApiEntries.summary: Resolves once the render pipeline is usable (immediately when headless) — and, under an initial `cy.load()`, once its **first chunk is drawn** (round 103; headless, once it is in the model). Rejects when no adapter can be had.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.style
v4ApiEntries.summary: Get the style engine, or set the stylesheet and return it.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.legend
v4ApiEntries.summary: Read the application's shared mapping and chart metadata. The returned JSON object is detached; changing it never alters this instance. Automatic domains expose their authored `auto` stops in the stylesheet and their current numeric stops here. `legendchange` fires after a committed snapshot changes, before `batchend` for a batch.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.compact
v4ApiEntries.summary: Slot-moving compaction, explicit form (round 19.5): move live elements down to a dense slot prefix so `highWater`, column capacity and pass-iteration widths shrink to the current graph instead of its peak.  A monotone remap keeps draw order — compaction is a visual no-op — and held refs/handles/listeners repair through forwarding (19.3).  The automatic dead-slot-ratio trigger covers the common shrink/churn profiles; this call is for deterministic timing (e.g. right after a bulk filter, before an animation).  Throws mid-batch; defers with a warning while a GPU force layout runs.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.startBatch
v4ApiEntries.summary: Open a batch: defer style application until the matching `endBatch()`. Pairs nest — only the outermost `endBatch()` flushes.  Prefer `batch( fn )`, which cannot leak a depth on an exception.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.endBatch
v4ApiEntries.summary: Close a batch.  At the outermost close the deferred work flushes as one bulk pass — filtered to elements still live, so adding and removing within the same batch costs nothing — and the automatic slot-compaction trigger gets its boundary check.  A sheet change during the batch applies once, as a diff against the sheet the columns were derived under (round 133); it writes the batch's additions in full, and the deferred data refreshes run after it unless the diff fell back to the whole-sheet pass, which subsumes them.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.batch
v4ApiEntries.summary: Run `fn` inside a `startBatch()`/`endBatch()` pair.  The batch closes even if `fn` throws, so this is the form to prefer.  As the outermost pair it is one transaction, `batchstart` … `batchend` (round 139); v4 has no rollback, so a throwing `fn` still ends in `batchend`, with the mutations that landed before the throw.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.layout
v4ApiEntries.summary: Make a layout over the whole graph.  The layout does not run until you call `.run()` on it.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.add
v4ApiEntries.summary: Add elements to the graph and return them as a collection.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.remove
v4ApiEntries.summary: Remove elements from the graph.  Removing a node removes its connected edges, and removing a compound parent removes its descendants.  Equivalent to `eles.remove()`.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.patch
v4ApiEntries.summary: Reconcile a fresh payload into the live graph **by id** (round 107): the payload is the next state of the *same* graph — the next query result, a server's refresh — and the patch computes what to add, remove and update, applies it as one batch, and returns what it did. A surviving element keeps selection, bypasses, running animations, listeners and scratch. Position follows the payload when carried; miniature state and its applied factor are adopted together with those current positions. The sheet, viewport and graph-level `data()` are never touched — elements only.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.load
v4ApiEntries.summary: **Progressive ingest** (round 103): load the graph chunk by chunk from an async iterable — a streamed response, a server's pages — and show a correct partial graph before the last byte arrives.  Each chunk is any input form (definition, columnar or wire); a chunk may name nodes an earlier chunk loaded — by id in the definition form, and through node references (`refs`) in the columnar and wire forms, which is what keeps a chunk's cut edges as cheap as its own.  A plain iterable (an array of chunks) works too.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.collection
v4ApiEntries.summary: An empty collection bound to this core — the accumulator for `union`/`add` chains.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.getElementById
v4ApiEntries.summary: Look up one element by id through the O(1) id index.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.elements
v4ApiEntries.summary: All elements, optionally filtered — nodes (in insertion order) then edges.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.nodes
v4ApiEntries.summary: The graph's nodes, optionally filtered.  Same query forms as `elements()`, restricted to the node group — and, with no query, the same memo (34.2).

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.edges
v4ApiEntries.summary: The graph's edges, optionally filtered.  Same query forms as `elements()`, restricted to the edge group — and, with no query, the same memo (34.2).

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.filter
v4ApiEntries.summary: Filter the whole graph.  Identical to `elements( query )`, kept for symmetry with `eles.filter()`.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.elementsInBox
v4ApiEntries.summary: Live, visible elements contained in the model-coordinate box (corners in any order): the box-selection query, answered by one columnar scan.  Nodes count when their bounding box lies fully inside; edges when both endpoint node centers do (v3's default 'contain' semantics, with straight-edge endpoints taken at the node centers).

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.emphasize
v4ApiEntries.summary: Emphasize exactly `eles` and dim everything else — the hover highlight every graph app implements, as view state rather than a restyle.  The call replaces the previous emphasis (only elements entering or leaving the set are written), so a hover handler is one line: `cy.emphasize( node.closedNeighborhood() )` on `mouseover`, `cy.unemphasize()` on `mouseout`.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.unemphasize
v4ApiEntries.summary: End the emphasis: clear the emphasized set and stop dimming.  A no-op when no emphasis is set.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.on
v4ApiEntries.summary: Listen for events on the core.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.one
v4ApiEntries.summary: Like `on()`, but the handler runs at most once and then removes itself.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.off
v4ApiEntries.summary: Stop listening.  Removing a delegated handler takes the same `( events, predicate, handler )` triple it was added with — predicates compare by function identity, so the predicate must be the same function object, not an equivalent one.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.removeAllListeners
v4ApiEntries.summary: Remove every listener on the core, including element-bound and delegated ones.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.emit
v4ApiEntries.summary: Emit an event on the core.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.promiseOn
v4ApiEntries.summary: Resolve once the next matching event fires — the promise form of `one()`.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.zoom
v4ApiEntries.summary: Get the zoom level, or set it.  Setting is a no-op while `zoomingEnabled()` is false, and the level is clamped to `zoomRange()`.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.pan
v4ApiEntries.summary: Get the pan offset, or set it.  Setting is a no-op while `panningEnabled()` is false.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.panBy
v4ApiEntries.summary: Shift the pan by a delta.  A no-op while `panningEnabled()` is false.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.fit
v4ApiEntries.summary: Pan and zoom so the given elements fill the viewport.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.center
v4ApiEntries.summary: Pan so the given elements are centred, leaving the zoom alone. Bounds include labels, as in `fit()`.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.animate
v4ApiEntries.summary: Animate the viewport (`pan`/`zoom`) over `duration` ms.  Element animation is on the collection (`eles.animate`).  Tweens are CPU-canonical; a data write / manual pan mid-animation is not prevented but will be overwritten by the next tick.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.animation
v4ApiEntries.summary: Like `animate`, but returns a handle with `play`/`stop`/`promise` — the viewport counterpart of `eles.animation`.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.animated
v4ApiEntries.summary: True while the viewport is animating.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.stop
v4ApiEntries.summary: Stop every running viewport animation (round 21: no queue — the v3 clearQueue argument is gone).

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.extent
v4ApiEntries.summary: The model-space rectangle currently visible, as `{ x1, y1, x2, y2, w, h }` — the inverse of the pan/zoom transform applied to the viewport box.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.renderedExtent
v4ApiEntries.summary: The rendered (on-screen) viewport rectangle.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.size
v4ApiEntries.summary: Rendered dimensions as { width, height }.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.minZoom
v4ApiEntries.summary: Get the minimum zoom, or set it.  Setting re-clamps the current zoom.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.maxZoom
v4ApiEntries.summary: Get the maximum zoom, or set it.  Setting re-clamps the current zoom.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.zoomRange
v4ApiEntries.summary: Set both zoom bounds; accepts (min, max) or { min, max }.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.viewport
v4ApiEntries.summary: Set zoom and/or pan together, emitting once.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.reset
v4ApiEntries.summary: Reset the viewport to zoom 1, pan (0, 0).

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.pick
v4ApiEntries.summary: Async GPU pick at a rendered (CSS px) position; resolves with the element under the point or null (always null when headless — the sync, node-only `cy.nodeAt()` computes headless).

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.nodeAt
v4ApiEntries.summary: The node at a rendered (CSS px) position, synchronously — or null (round 75.4, #1209).  The sync half of the pick pair: `cy.pick()` is async because an edge hit is a GPU question, while a node hit is answered on the CPU from the canonical columns, in the same microtask — the pick the pointer's own pan-vs-grab decision trusts.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.viewportCounts
v4ApiEntries.summary: How many nodes and edges the renderer draws — the visible counts of the next frame, after the viewport test, `visibility` and the level of detail (round 75.6, #2283).  Async because the counts live on the GPU: the cull writes them into its indirect draw arguments, and this reads them back.  Schedules a frame when nothing is pending, so it resolves on a graph at rest too; concurrent calls share one readback. Compound parents count as nodes; labels are not counted (the glyph streams count glyphs, not labels).

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.stats
v4ApiEntries.summary: The renderer's frame statistics, or null when headless.  The snapshot carries the frame timings, cache hit rates and pass counters — note that `cpuFrameMs` is encode/submit cost only (submission is fire-and-forget), so reconcile fps against `gpuFrameMs`.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.resize
v4ApiEntries.summary: Re-measure the container, redraw and emit `'resize'` (the redraw is a no-op when headless; the event still fires).

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.png
v4ApiEntries.summary: Export the rendered graph as a PNG.  Async — the pixels live on the GPU (offscreen render + readback), unlike v3's synchronous base64 form; every output form resolves through the returned promise. Options as in v3: `bg`, `full`, `scale` or `maxWidth`/`maxHeight`, `output` ('base64uri' default | 'base64' | 'blob'; 'blob-promise' is an accepted alias of 'blob').  Headless instances reject — there is no renderer to export from.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.jpg
v4ApiEntries.summary: Export as JPEG: as {@link png}, plus `quality` (0..1) and a white default `bg` (JPEG has no alpha channel).

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.data
v4ApiEntries.section: Graph-level data & scratch (plain objects, not columns)
v4ApiEntries.summary: Graph-level data — read all, read one key, or write.  This is a plain object, not a columnar sidecar (which is `ele.data()`).  It **is** carried by the wire format since round 39.2: `serialize()` writes it and `options.elements` applies it, while `cy.add( buffer )` deliberately ignores it.  Writing emits `data`.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.removeData
v4ApiEntries.section: Graph-level data & scratch (plain objects, not columns)
v4ApiEntries.summary: Delete graph-level data keys.  Emits `data` when anything was removed.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.scratch
v4ApiEntries.section: Graph-level data & scratch (plain objects, not columns)
v4ApiEntries.summary: Graph-level scratchpad — like `data()`, but for transient state that is never exported and never emits.  Namespace your keys (an extension convention: `'_myExtension'`).

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.removeScratch
v4ApiEntries.section: Graph-level data & scratch (plain objects, not columns)
v4ApiEntries.summary: Delete graph-level scratch keys.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.autolock
v4ApiEntries.summary: Get or set whether every node is locked (immovable) regardless of its own `locked` flag — the graph-wide override.  Turned on mid-tween, every running position tween holds where it got to (round 144), as a node locked mid-tween does.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.autoungrabify
v4ApiEntries.summary: Get or set whether every node is ungrabbable regardless of its own `grabbable` flag.  Unlike `autolock()`, this blocks only user dragging; programmatic position writes still apply.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.autounselectify
v4ApiEntries.summary: Get or set whether every element is unselectable regardless of its own `selectable` flag.  Programmatic `select()` still applies.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.panningEnabled
v4ApiEntries.summary: Get or set whether panning is allowed at all — programmatic `pan()` included.  Use `userPanningEnabled()` to block only the gesture.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.userPanningEnabled
v4ApiEntries.summary: Get or set whether the user may pan by dragging.  Programmatic `pan()` is unaffected.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.zoomingEnabled
v4ApiEntries.summary: Get or set whether zooming is allowed at all — programmatic `zoom()` included.  Use `userZoomingEnabled()` to block only the gesture.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.userZoomingEnabled
v4ApiEntries.summary: Get or set whether the user may zoom by wheel or pinch. Programmatic `zoom()` is unaffected.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.boxSelectionIncludesLabels
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether box selection considers label boxes as well as node bodies (round 16.5; v3's box-select-labels, reshaped as a core option — default off).  Its sense **follows `boxSelectionMode`**: under `'contain'` the label box must *also* be inside the band, under `'overlap'` a label that merely crosses the band is *enough*.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.boxSelectionMode
v4ApiEntries.summary: What the box-selection gesture counts as caught: `'contain'` (default, v3's) selects only elements wholly inside the band; `'overlap'` selects anything the band touches — a node whose box intersects it, an edge any part of whose drawn path crosses it. Round 39.1.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.boxSelectionEnabled
v4ApiEntries.summary: Get or set whether the box-selection gesture is available.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.pointerCursors
v4ApiEntries.summary: Get or set whether the canvas writes CSS cursors for the gesture affordances (round 89): `grab` over a draggable node and `grabbing` while it or the background is being dragged, `pointer` over any other interactive element, `crosshair` while box-selecting.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.selectionType
v4ApiEntries.summary: How user selection composes: 'single' (a tap or box replaces the selection) or 'additive' (taps toggle and boxes add, as if a multiple-select key were always held).

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.multiClickDebounceTime
v4ApiEntries.summary: The dbltap/onetap debounce window in ms (v3 parity; default 250).

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.wheelSensitivity
v4ApiEntries.summary: Wheel-zoom sensitivity: a multiplier on the zoom-per-wheel-tick exponent (v3 parity; default 1).  Non-default values warn once per instance, as v3 does — a custom sensitivity tuned on one mouse/OS zooms unnaturally on others.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.wheelBehavior
v4ApiEntries.summary: What a wheel over the canvas does (round 75.5): `'zoom'` (the default, v3's) zooms about the cursor; `'pan'` pans by the wheel's delta and emits `scrollpan`, while a ctrl- or meta-wheel — the encoding a trackpad pinch arrives in — still zooms; `'modifier-zoom'` leaves the plain wheel to the page (it scrolls past the graph) and zooms only on a ctrl- or meta-wheel.  Every mode honours the toggles (`userZoomingEnabled` gates a zoom, `userPanningEnabled` a pan), and a wheel the settings leave inert is **not** `preventDefault()`ed, so the page scrolls — v3's contract, restored in the same round.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.desktopTapThreshold
v4ApiEntries.summary: Css px a mouse/pen press may move and still count as a tap (v3 parity; default 4).

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.touchTapThreshold
v4ApiEntries.summary: Css px a touch press may move and still count as a tap (v3 parity; default 8).

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.tapholdDuration
v4ApiEntries.summary: Unmoved-press duration before 'taphold' fires, ms (default 500 — v3's constant, configurable in v4).

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.isReady
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether the render pipeline is usable yet.  Always true on a headless instance; on a rendered one this flips when `cy.ready` resolves.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.headless
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether this instance has no container and therefore no GPU — the Node-testable mode, in which every model API works and the render, pick and image-export paths are no-ops or reject.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.styleEnabled
v4ApiEntries.summary: Always true: v4 has no style-disabled mode, since the columnar model derives geometry from stored style channels rather than treating style as an optional layer.  Kept so v3 code that checks it works.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.hasCompoundNodes
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether any node currently has a parent.  Worth checking because the compound tier changes paint evaluation and draw order; the renderer pays nothing for compounds while this is false.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.hasElementWithId
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether an element with this id exists, via the O(1) id index — cheaper than `getElementById( id ).nonempty()` because no handle is materialized.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.window
v4ApiEntries.summary: The `window` this instance renders into, or null when there is no DOM (Node).  v3 parity, for extensions that need the hosting realm.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.options
v4ApiEntries.summary: The options the instance was constructed with.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.serialize
v4ApiEntries.summary: Export the live graph as the binary wire format (the buffer `options.elements`/`add()` accept directly): the columnar counterpart of `json()`.  Carries ids, positions, selection state, the data() sidecar and — since round 39.2 — graph-level `data()`; style, viewport and scratch are not part of the wire.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.json
v4ApiEntries.summary: Export the graph as a plain object — elements, stylesheet, viewport, gating flags and graph-level data.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.clone
v4ApiEntries.summary: Make an independent instance holding a copy of this graph (round 106) — the way to show one graph in two places, e.g. a minimap beside the main view.  A second view is a second instance, never a second renderer over one model: each clone has its own sheet, viewport, selection, hover, listeners and `png()`.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.unmount
v4ApiEntries.summary: Detach the renderer: the instance becomes headless (the model is CPU-canonical, so nothing is lost).  No-op when already headless.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.mount
v4ApiEntries.summary: (Re)attach a renderer to a container.  Re-mounting to a different container unmounts first; the fresh renderer re-uploads every column from the CPU-canonical model and rebuilds all glyph runs.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.container
v4ApiEntries.summary: The DOM element this instance renders into, or null when headless or unmounted.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.width
v4ApiEntries.summary: The rendered width in CSS px.  Headless instances report the configured `headlessWidth` (default 800), so viewport maths works without a DOM.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.height
v4ApiEntries.summary: The rendered height in CSS px.  Headless instances report the configured `headlessHeight` (default 600).

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.destroy
v4ApiEntries.summary: Tear the instance down: emit `destroy`, drop every listener, and release the pointer handler and the renderer (with its GPU resources).  Idempotent.  The store is left intact but the instance must not be used afterwards.

v4ApiEntries.name: cy.destroyed
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether `destroy()` has run.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.length
v4ApiEntries.summary: How many elements this collection holds.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.cy
v4ApiEntries.summary: The core this collection belongs to.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.collection
v4ApiEntries.summary: An empty collection in the same core.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.hasElementWithId
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether this collection contains an element with the given id.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.indexOf
v4ApiEntries.summary: Index of an element within this collection.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.indexOfId
v4ApiEntries.summary: Position of the element with this id within the collection.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.size
v4ApiEntries.summary: The number of elements — the method form of `length`.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.empty
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether the collection holds no elements.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.nonempty
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether the collection holds at least one element.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.forEach
v4ApiEntries.summary: Call `fn` for each element.  Returning `false` from the callback stops the iteration early, as in v3.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.toArray
v4ApiEntries.summary: The elements as a plain array of length-1 collections.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.slice
v4ApiEntries.summary: A sub-range of the collection, with `Array#slice` semantics (negative indices count from the end).

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.sort
v4ApiEntries.summary: A copy sorted by a comparator.  Note that sort order is a property of the *collection*, not of drawing: v4 draw order is structural and there is no `z-index`.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.eq
v4ApiEntries.summary: The element at an index, as a length-1 collection.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.first
v4ApiEntries.summary: The first element, as a length-1 collection.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.last
v4ApiEntries.summary: The last element, as a length-1 collection.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.map
v4ApiEntries.summary: Map each element through `fn` into a plain array.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.some
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether any element satisfies the predicate.  Short-circuits.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.every
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether every element satisfies the predicate.  Short-circuits, and is vacuously true for an empty collection.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.id
v4ApiEntries.summary: The first element's id.  Cached on the handle, so it stays readable after the element is removed.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.group
v4ApiEntries.summary: The first element's group.  Cached on the handle, so it stays readable after removal.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.json
v4ApiEntries.summary: Plain-object form of the first element (undefined when empty).

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.jsons
v4ApiEntries.summary: Plain-object form of every element.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.isNode
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether the first element is a node.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.isEdge
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether the first element is an edge.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.isLoop
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether the first element is a self-loop — an edge whose source and target are the same node.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.isSimple
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether the first element is a non-loop edge.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.removed
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether the first element has been removed from the graph.  A removed element's handle stays usable — reads are no-ops or undefined, and the cached `id()`/`group()` remain readable.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.inside
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether the first element is still in the graph — the complement of `removed()`.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.same
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether both collections hold exactly the same elements, ignoring order.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.anySame
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether the two collections share at least one element.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.contains
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether every element of `other` is also in this collection.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.allAreNeighbors
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether every element of `other` is in this collection's neighborhood.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.allAre
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether every element matches the criterion.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.is
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether any element matches the criterion.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.union
v4ApiEntries.summary: The union of the two collections, deduped.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.difference
v4ApiEntries.summary: This collection's elements that are not in `other`.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.intersection
v4ApiEntries.summary: The elements present in both collections.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.symmetricDifference
v4ApiEntries.summary: The elements in exactly one of the two collections.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.filter
v4ApiEntries.summary: The subset matching the criterion.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.nodes
v4ApiEntries.summary: The nodes in this collection, optionally filtered.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.edges
v4ApiEntries.summary: The edges in this collection, optionally filtered.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.getElementById
v4ApiEntries.summary: Find a member by id.  This is a linear scan of the collection; use `cy.$id( id )` for the O(1) whole-graph index.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.absoluteComplement
v4ApiEntries.summary: All elements of the graph not in this collection.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.diff
v4ApiEntries.summary: Three-way set difference against another collection.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.reduce
v4ApiEntries.summary: Fold the collection into a single value.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.max
v4ApiEntries.summary: The element maximizing `valFn`, with its value.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.min
v4ApiEntries.summary: The element minimizing `valFn`, with its value.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.position
v4ApiEntries.summary: Get or set the first element's model-space position (nodes only).

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.positions
v4ApiEntries.summary: Set every node's position, from a constant or per-element function.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.animate
v4ApiEntries.summary: Animate these elements' style and/or position to explicit targets over `duration` ms, easing the normalized time.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.animation
v4ApiEntries.summary: Build an animation for these elements without starting it.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.delay
v4ApiEntries.summary: A no-op tween — a timed pause that touches no channels, so it composes with any running animation (round 21: use `delayAnimation().play()` + await to sequence).

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.delayAnimation
v4ApiEntries.summary: Like {@link delay}, but returns the handle instead of chaining.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.animated
v4ApiEntries.summary: True when any of these elements has a running animation.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.stop
v4ApiEntries.summary: Stop every running animation on these elements (round 21: no queue — the v3 clearQueue argument is gone).

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.shift
v4ApiEntries.summary: Offset positions by a vector or along one axis.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.relativePosition
v4ApiEntries.summary: Compound-relative position: the model position minus the immediate parent's (derived) position — the model position for orphans and compound-free graphs (round 14.3, v3 semantics).

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.renderedPosition
v4ApiEntries.summary: Get or set the first element's position in rendered (CSS px) space — `position()` put through the current pan and zoom.  Writing unprojects back to model space, so the element lands under the given screen point at the current viewport.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.width
v4ApiEntries.summary: The first element's width — a node's model-space width, or an edge's stroke width.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.height
v4ApiEntries.summary: The first element's height — a node's model-space height, or an edge's stroke width (as in v3, where an edge's `height` is its width).

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.data
v4ApiEntries.summary: data() over the sidecar columns.  `id` (and `source`/`target` on edges) are first-class and immutable — reading them works, writing them throws.  Setters apply to every element in the collection and emit `data` per element; a write refreshes data-mapped labels. The whole-object read returns a built snapshot, not the store's internals — and the *same* snapshot until a data write (or a reparent/re-point) invalidates it, so mutating it never corrupts the store but is visible to the mutator until the next write (v3 hands out its live internal object here, where mutation corrupts the actual store — v4's exposure is strictly narrower).

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.removeData
v4ApiEntries.summary: Remove sidecar data keys.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.scratch
v4ApiEntries.summary: Per-element scratchpad (plain JS, not a column): `scratch()` reads the first element's whole object, `scratch(ns)` one namespace, `scratch(ns, val)` / `scratch(obj)` write to every element.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.removeScratch
v4ApiEntries.summary: Delete scratchpad keys from every element.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.style
v4ApiEntries.summary: Resolved style read off the stored channels — all of the first element's group props.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.removeStyle
v4ApiEntries.summary: Remove per-element style bypasses from every element (round 63.4 — v3's `removeStyle`).  The sheet-resolved values return through the normal apply, transitions included.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.renderedStyle
v4ApiEntries.summary: Like `style()`, but with length props (width, height, border-width, font-size) scaled into rendered (on-screen) px by the zoom.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.numericStyle
v4ApiEntries.summary: The numeric value of a numeric style prop.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.effectiveOpacity
v4ApiEntries.summary: The rendered opacity: a node's own opacity times its ancestors' (v3's product rule — the store keeps the folded value in the column, round 14.4); an edge's own opacity (edges have no parent).

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.transparent
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether the first element is fully transparent — its effective opacity, with compound ancestors folded in, is exactly 0.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.takesUpSpace
v4ApiEntries.summary: The space tier (round 22): shown elements occupy space — they join bb/fit and size their compound parents — even when `visibility: 'hidden'` keeps them from rendering.  display-tier hide() clears it.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.interactive
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether the element can be interacted with: visible and not pointer-transparent (`events: 'no'` — round 20.2).

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.label
v4ApiEntries.summary: The node's resolved label text ('' when none); read-only in the prototype.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.padding
v4ApiEntries.summary: v3-parity accessor: node padding.  Leaves have no padding in v4 (no compound-free `padding` prop); parents answer the resolved auto-bounds padding (round 14.3).

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.paddedWidth
v4ApiEntries.summary: The drawn box: core dims + 2 x padding (v3's paddedWidth).

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.paddedHeight
v4ApiEntries.summary: The drawn box height: content height plus twice the padding (v3's `paddedHeight`).  Identical to `height()` for leaves, which have no padding.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.outerWidth
v4ApiEntries.summary: The full drawn width including the border — padded width plus the border width.  This is the box bounds and endpoint clipping use.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.outerHeight
v4ApiEntries.summary: The full drawn height including the border.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.boundingBox
v4ApiEntries.summary: The model-space box enclosing every element of the collection.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.labelBoundingBox
v4ApiEntries.summary: The exact laid label boxes of this collection's elements, unioned (round 16.4 — the v4 form of v3's text-metrics surface): node labels at their anchors, edge mid-labels at the drawn midpoint, end labels conservatively about their endpoint.  Empty (zero) when nothing is labelled.  Headless dims are estimates (recorded).

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.renderedBoundingBox
v4ApiEntries.summary: `boundingBox()` transformed into rendered (on-screen) coordinates.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.renderedWidth
v4ApiEntries.summary: `width()` scaled by the current zoom — the on-screen width in CSS px.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.renderedHeight
v4ApiEntries.summary: `height()` scaled by the current zoom.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.renderedOuterWidth
v4ApiEntries.summary: `outerWidth()` scaled by the current zoom.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.renderedOuterHeight
v4ApiEntries.summary: `outerHeight()` scaled by the current zoom.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.midpoint
v4ApiEntries.summary: Midpoint of the edge: the curve/route midpoint for curved edges (v3's rs.mid rules per family), the endpoint-center average for straight ones.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.renderedMidpoint
v4ApiEntries.summary: `midpoint()` in rendered (CSS px) space.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.sourceEndpoint
v4ApiEntries.summary: The edge's source-side endpoint in model space, resolved through the route evaluator — so it accounts for curve family, node boundary clipping, haystack offsets and any manual `source-endpoint`.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.targetEndpoint
v4ApiEntries.summary: The edge's target-side endpoint in model space, resolved through the route evaluator — so it accounts for curve family, node boundary clipping, haystack offsets and any manual `target-endpoint`.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.renderedSourceEndpoint
v4ApiEntries.summary: `sourceEndpoint()` in rendered (CSS px) space.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.renderedTargetEndpoint
v4ApiEntries.summary: `targetEndpoint()` in rendered (CSS px) space.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.controlPoints
v4ApiEntries.summary: The edge's curve control points (model coords): one for a bundled bezier, two for a self-loop, the control list for an unbundled bezier, undefined otherwise — v3's getControlPoints surface (segments/taxi answer segmentPoints() instead).

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.renderedControlPoints
v4ApiEntries.summary: `controlPoints()` in rendered (CSS px) space.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.segmentPoints
v4ApiEntries.summary: The edge's segment points (model coords) — v3's getSegmentPoints: defined for segments *and* taxi edges (taxi derives its points), undefined otherwise.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.renderedSegmentPoints
v4ApiEntries.summary: `segmentPoints()` in rendered (CSS px) space.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.selected
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether the first element is selected.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.selectable
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether the first element may be selected by the user.  The graph-wide `cy.autounselectify()` overrides this for user gestures.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.select
v4ApiEntries.summary: Select every selectable element, emitting `select` for each one that changed.  Unselectable elements are skipped.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.unselect
v4ApiEntries.summary: Deselect every element, emitting `unselect` for each one that changed.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.selectify
v4ApiEntries.summary: Make these elements selectable.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.unselectify
v4ApiEntries.summary: Make these elements unselectable.  Does not deselect them; call `unselect()` for that.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.grabbable
v4ApiEntries.summary: Pannable elements are not draggable, so pannable overrides grabbable (as in v3).

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.grabbed
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether the first element is currently held by a drag gesture.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.grabify
v4ApiEntries.summary: Make these elements grabbable.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.ungrabify
v4ApiEntries.summary: Make these elements ungrabbable — the user can no longer drag them, while programmatic position writes still apply.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.visible
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether the first element renders (round 22: the derived FLAG_DRAWN — shown AND not `visibility: 'hidden'` on self or, for nodes, any ancestor; edges additionally fold their endpoints, v3's rule).  The renderer's cull pass and CPU picking mask on the same bit, so an element that is not visible() neither draws nor picks.  For space-tier state (in the bb, sizing its compound parent) see `takesUpSpace()` — an invisible element keeps its space.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.hidden
v4ApiEntries.summary: The complement of `visible()`.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.show
v4ApiEntries.summary: Show these elements — the **display tier**, v3's structural `display: element`.  Shown elements take up space again, rejoin bounds and fit, and re-fan their bezier bundles.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.hide
v4ApiEntries.summary: Hide these elements structurally — v3's `display: none`.  They stop drawing and picking, leave the bounding box and their ancestors' auto-bounds, and their bezier bundles re-fan without them. Descendants of a hidden node are gated too.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.locked
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether the first element is locked — immovable, by layouts, position writes and position tweens alike (one rule since round 114.3: every layout holds a locked node where it is and keeps it in the layout's structure; force treats it as an obstacle its settle separates the others from).  A locked child stays where it is when its compound parent is positioned, shifted or dragged — its own subtree with it — and the parent re-derives about the stayers and the movers (116.3, v3's rule).  True for every node while `cy.autolock( true )` is set, as in v3; the flag column alone is what `{ locked: true }` filters read.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.lock
v4ApiEntries.summary: Lock these elements against movement.  A node locked mid-tween holds where its position tween got to (round 144, as v3's animation step skips a locked node); the rest of the animation — other nodes, and this node's paint channels — runs on, and unlocking does not resume it.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.unlock
v4ApiEntries.summary: Unlock these elements.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.active
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether the first element is in the transient pressed ("active") state.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.pannable
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether dragging the first element pans the graph instead of grabbing it.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.panify
v4ApiEntries.summary: Make dragging these elements pan the viewport instead of moving them.  Pannable overrides grabbable, as in v3.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.unpanify
v4ApiEntries.summary: Stop these elements from panning the viewport when dragged, so a grabbable one becomes draggable again.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.emphasized
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether the first element is in the current emphasis — the set the last `cy.emphasize( eles )` named.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.remove
v4ApiEntries.summary: Remove these elements from the graph; incident edges of removed nodes cascade.  Already-removed elements are skipped (no second `remove` event).

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.move
v4ApiEntries.summary: Move elements in place, keeping slot, id and data: `{ parent }` re-parents nodes (null orphans them; the compound move, round 14.2 — emits `moveout` before and `move` after per changed node), while `{ source, target }` re-points edges.  As in v3 the modes are exclusive — a `parent` key takes precedence.  An unknown parent id is a silent no-op (v3); a cyclic assignment warns and drops (the hierarchy rule).

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.source
v4ApiEntries.summary: The source node of the first edge.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.target
v4ApiEntries.summary: The target node of the first edge.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.sources
v4ApiEntries.summary: The source nodes of every edge in the collection, deduped.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.targets
v4ApiEntries.summary: The target nodes of every edge in the collection, deduped.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.connectedEdges
v4ApiEntries.summary: Every edge incident on the nodes in this collection, deduped — answered off the CSR adjacency index, so it is O(incident edges) rather than a scan.  Loops appear once.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.connectedNodes
v4ApiEntries.summary: The endpoint nodes of every edge in this collection, deduped.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.outgoers
v4ApiEntries.summary: The immediate outgoing neighbourhood: the edges leaving these nodes plus the nodes they point at.  One hop only — use `successors()` for the transitive closure.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.incomers
v4ApiEntries.summary: The immediate incoming neighbourhood: the edges arriving at these nodes plus the nodes they come from.  One hop only — use `predecessors()` for the transitive closure.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.neighborhood
v4ApiEntries.summary: The *open* neighbourhood: the incident edges and the nodes on their far ends, ignoring edge direction, excluding the collection's own elements.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.closedNeighborhood
v4ApiEntries.summary: The open neighbourhood plus this collection's own nodes.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.parent
v4ApiEntries.summary: Immediate parents of every node in the collection (unique).  v4 always returns a proper collection — v3's single-element raw-ref shortcut (which also ignored the selector argument) is not ported.   *

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.parents
v4ApiEntries.summary: All ancestors, level by level: every nearest parent first, then the grandparents, and so on (v3's iterated-parent() order).   *

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.children
v4ApiEntries.summary: Direct children of every node, in link order per parent.   *

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.descendants
v4ApiEntries.summary: The subtree below every node in pre-order, excluding the nodes themselves.   *

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.collapse
v4ApiEntries.summary: Scale each compound parent’s descendants into a miniature around the parent’s current centre. Pass `{ duration, easing }` to animate the scale; without options, the operation is immediate. The original nodes, edges and explicit visibility state remain unchanged.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.expand
v4ApiEntries.summary: Restore each collapsed compound parent’s descendants by reversing its currently applied scale around the parent’s current centre. Pass `{ duration, easing }` to animate the restoration; without options, the operation is immediate.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.siblings
v4ApiEntries.summary: Nodes sharing a parent with the collection's nodes, excluding them; orphans are nobody's siblings (v3).   *

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.orphans
v4ApiEntries.summary: The collection's nodes without a parent.   *

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.nonorphans
v4ApiEntries.summary: The collection's nodes that have a parent.   *

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.commonAncestors
v4ApiEntries.summary: Ancestors common to every element, closest first (an edge in the collection has no ancestors, so it empties the result — v3).   *

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.isParent
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether the first element is a node with at least one child.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.isChildless
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether the first element is a node with no children.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.isChild
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether the first element is a node with a parent.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.collapsed
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether the first live node is a collapsed compound parent.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.insideCollapsed
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether the first live node has a collapsed strict ancestor. The collapsed parent itself answers false.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.isOrphan
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether the first element is a node without a parent.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.roots
v4ApiEntries.summary: Collection nodes with no non-loop incoming edge (whole-graph incidence, as in v3).   *

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.leaves
v4ApiEntries.summary: Collection nodes with no non-loop outgoing edge.   *

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.successors
v4ApiEntries.summary: Everything reachable by following outgoing edges, transitively — the edges and nodes of the forward closure, excluding these nodes themselves (unless a cycle reaches them).

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.predecessors
v4ApiEntries.summary: Everything that reaches these nodes by following incoming edges, transitively.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.edgesWith
v4ApiEntries.summary: The edges connecting this collection's nodes with `others`, in either direction.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.edgesTo
v4ApiEntries.summary: The edges running *from* this collection's nodes *to* `others` — `edgesWith()` restricted by direction.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.parallelEdges
v4ApiEntries.summary: The edges sharing endpoints with these edges, in either direction — including each edge itself.  These are the edges a bezier bundle fans apart.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.codirectedEdges
v4ApiEntries.summary: The parallel edges pointing the same way — same source and same target — including each edge itself.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.components
v4ApiEntries.summary: Connected components within this collection (undirected), each as a collection of the reached nodes plus the collection's edges internal to that component.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.component
v4ApiEntries.summary: The whole-graph connected component containing the first element.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.layoutDimensions
v4ApiEntries.summary: Node dimensions for layout spacing, as v3's layoutDimensions — the body, plus the label box under `nodeDimensionsIncludeLabels: true` (114.1 made labels the default; 115 restored v3's body-only default).

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.layoutPositions
v4ApiEntries.summary: Apply a layout's position function to this collection's nodes with the standard layout options (spacingFactor, transform, fit/zoom/pan, animate) and the layoutstart/layoutready/layoutstop event flow — v3's helper. With `animate: true` the viewport animates concurrently (a fit targets the bounding box at the *final* positions, as v3 does).

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.layout
v4ApiEntries.summary: A layout scoped to this collection.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.breadthFirstSearch
v4ApiEntries.summary: Breadth-first search over this collection's subgraph. Roots are visited in breadth-first order. Multiple callback roots are visited in reverse input order because the initial queue prepends each root; with no roots, the result is empty.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.depthFirstSearch
v4ApiEntries.summary: Depth-first search over this collection's subgraph. It shares the root, callback, direction and result contract of `breadthFirstSearch`, but explores the most recently discovered branch first.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.dijkstra
v4ApiEntries.summary: Compute single-source shortest paths from a root over this collection's subgraph using Dijkstra's algorithm. The caller is responsible for using non-negative edge weights; v4 does not validate the weight function's mathematical properties.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.aStar
v4ApiEntries.summary: Find an A* path between two nodes in this collection's subgraph. The heuristic defaults to zero, reducing the search to Dijkstra's ordering. The search closes nodes without reopening them; shortest-path guarantees require non-negative costs and a consistent heuristic. v4 does not validate those mathematical properties.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.bellmanFord
v4ApiEntries.summary: Compute single-source shortest paths with Bellman–Ford. Unlike `dijkstra()`, this algorithm supports negative edge weights and reports reachable negative-weight cycles.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.floydWarshall
v4ApiEntries.summary: Floyd–Warshall all-pairs shortest paths.  O(n³) — for a single source prefer `dijkstra`/`bellmanFord`.  Async (round 65): the expensive whole-graph tier returns promises, and `executor` ('cpu' | 'gpu' | 'auto', default 'auto'; 'workers' runs the reference on one pool worker, round 129.1) picks where the maths runs; 'cpu' is the reproducible reference.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.kruskal
v4ApiEntries.summary: Build a minimum spanning forest of this collection, treating its edges as undirected. Equal-weight edges retain collection order. Disconnected input produces one tree per connected component.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.tarjanStronglyConnected
v4ApiEntries.summary: Partition this collection's directed subgraph into strongly connected components. Traversal follows edge direction; self-loops do not join otherwise separate nodes. The implementation is iterative, so deep graphs do not consume the JavaScript call stack.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.hopcroftTarjanBiconnected
v4ApiEntries.summary: Find undirected biconnected components and articulation points in this collection's subgraph. The component partition follows the v4 port's parent-edge rule: all edges back to the DFS parent are skipped, including parallel edges.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.hierholzer
v4ApiEntries.summary: Find an Eulerian trail or circuit over this collection's edges. The directed mode checks directed degree balance; the default treats edges as undirected. A requested root must be a valid starting node for the trail.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.kargerStein
v4ApiEntries.summary: Estimate an undirected global minimum cut with the randomized Karger–Stein contraction algorithm. Connected input is required for its guarantee. Random choices mean repeated runs may produce different partitions; the minimum-cut result is probabilistic.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.pageRank
v4ApiEntries.summary: PageRank over the (directed) subgraph.  Async (round 65): returns a promise, and `executor` ('cpu' | 'gpu' | 'auto', default 'auto'; 'workers' runs the reference on one pool worker, round 129.1) picks where the power method runs; 'cpu' is the reproducible reference.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.degreeCentrality
v4ApiEntries.summary: Compute Opsahl's generalized degree for one node in this collection. `alpha` interpolates between counting edges (0) and summing their weights (1); intermediate values combine both. Directed results separate incoming and outgoing degree.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.degreeCentralityNormalized
v4ApiEntries.summary: Compute each node's Opsahl generalized degree and normalize against the maximum in this collection. Directed in- and out-degree are normalized independently. Nodes outside the collection's captured subgraph read as zero.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.closenessCentrality
v4ApiEntries.summary: Closeness centrality of one node — the reciprocal of its summed shortest-path distances to the rest of the collection.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.closenessCentralityNormalized
v4ApiEntries.summary: Closeness centrality for every node, normalized to [0, 1].  Async (round 69): the whole-collection form is the all-pairs tier, so like `floydWarshall` it returns a promise and `executor` ('cpu' | 'gpu' | 'workers' | 'auto', default 'auto') picks where it runs; 'cpu' is the reproducible reference.  Unweighted runs walk a BFS per source, O(n·(n+E)) (round 72.3) — on the worker pool too (round 74: one source range per worker, bit-identical to 'cpu'; under 'auto' a sparse graph takes the pool first from 512 nodes, since it measured ahead of the GPU's batched BFS at every size, and a dense one the GPU first); weighted runs relax Floyd–Warshall, O(n³), and take the offload lane (round 129.1: one pool worker).  The single-root `closenessCentrality` stays synchronous.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.betweennessCentrality
v4ApiEntries.summary: Betweenness centrality — how often each node lies on shortest paths between other pairs.  Async (round 65): returns a promise, and `executor` ('cpu' | 'gpu' | 'workers' | 'auto', default 'auto') picks where the Brandes sweep runs.  Weighted runs have no GPU path: 'auto' takes the worker pool (round 74 — one source range per worker, f64-tight to 'cpu' and bit-stable across pool sizes) from 128 nodes and an explicit 'gpu' rejects; unweighted runs keep the GPU first under 'auto', then the pool from 256 nodes where no adapter fits.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.katzCentrality
v4ApiEntries.summary: Katz centrality — attenuated walk counting, where a node is central when many short walks end at it and a walk of length k is worth alphaᵏ.  Async (round 69): returns a promise, and `executor` ('cpu' | 'gpu' | 'auto', default 'auto'; 'workers' runs the reference on one pool worker, round 129.1) picks where the iteration runs; like `pageRank`, 'auto' always uses the sparse CPU iteration and the GPU path serves an explicit 'gpu'.  v4-only — v3 has no counterpart.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.triangleCount
v4ApiEntries.summary: Triangle counting: per-node triangle counts, local clustering coefficients, and the collection's transitivity, read over the simple undirected graph (direction ignored, parallel edges collapsed, loops excluded).  Async (round 69): returns a promise, and `executor` ('cpu' | 'gpu' | 'auto', default 'auto'; 'workers' runs the reference on one pool worker, round 129.1) picks where the counting runs — under 'auto' the GPU's A²∘A matmul is used only on graphs dense enough to beat the CPU's sparse walk (a mean degree of 64, round 72.6).  v4-only — v3 has no counterpart.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.neighborhoodSimilarity
v4ApiEntries.summary: Neighborhood similarity — pairwise Jaccard, cosine or overlap coefficients over neighbor sets (deduped; loops excluded; `directed: true` compares out-neighborhoods).  The result is all-pairs, so it holds O(n²) counts like `floydWarshall`.  Async (round 69): returns a promise, and `executor` ('cpu' | 'gpu' | 'auto', default 'auto') picks where the shared-neighbor counts are computed — under 'auto' the GPU's A·Aᵀ matmul is used only on graphs dense enough to beat the CPU's wedge walk (a mean degree of 64, round 72.6).  v4-only — v3 has no counterpart.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.simRank
v4ApiEntries.summary: SimRank — "two nodes are similar when their neighbors are similar", the Jeh–Widom recursive fixed point, iterated as dense products S′ = C·Q·S·Qᵀ.  Async (round 70): returns a promise, and `executor` ('cpu' | 'gpu' | 'auto', default 'auto'; 'workers' runs the reference on one pool worker, round 129.1) picks where the iteration runs — under 'auto' the GPU from 256 nodes at any density (round 72.6 measured it ahead everywhere).  The undirected default compares all neighbors; `directed: true` compares the classic in-neighborhoods.  All-pairs (O(n²) memory).  v4-only — v3 has no counterpart.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.randomWalkWithRestart
v4ApiEntries.summary: Random walk with restart — network propagation from a `seeds` collection: a walker follows edges with probability 1−c and restarts at the seeds with probability c, and the stationary distribution scores every node by proximity to the seeds.  Async (round 70); the vector iteration is O(E) per step on the CPU, so there is no GPU path — an explicit `executor: 'gpu'` rejects and points at `randomWalkWithRestartProximity`.  On directed graphs a node with no out-edges absorbs the walk (scores can sum below 1). v4-only — v3 has no counterpart.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.randomWalkWithRestartProximity
v4ApiEntries.summary: All-pairs random-walk-with-restart proximity — the full matrix S = c·(I − (1−c)·W)⁻¹, whose column s is the walk restarting at s.  Async (round 70): `executor` ('cpu' | 'gpu' | 'workers' | 'auto', default 'auto') picks between one sparse solve per column on the CPU, the same solves spread over the worker pool (round 74 — bit-identical to 'cpu') and the dense Neumann iteration on the GPU — under 'auto' the GPU from 256 nodes at any density (round 72.6 measured it ahead everywhere), else the pool from 128. All-pairs (O(n²) memory).  v4-only — v3 has no counterpart.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.heatDiffusion
v4ApiEntries.summary: Heat diffusion from a `seeds` collection: unit heat spread over the seeds flows along edges for `time`, through the kernel exp(−t·L) of the weighted Laplacian.  Total heat is conserved under the default `laplacian: 'combinatorial'`; `'normalized'` (round 72.4) diffuses over I − D^{-½}AD^{-½} instead, whose spectrum is bounded whatever the degrees — hubs neither hoard nor flood — at the price of conservation.  Async (round 70); the vector form is O(E) per series term on the CPU, so there is no GPU path — an explicit `executor: 'gpu'` rejects and points at `heatKernel`.  Edges are read undirected with positive weights. v4-only — v3 has no counterpart.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.heatKernel
v4ApiEntries.summary: The all-pairs heat kernel exp(−t·L) — `heat(from, to)` is the heat at `to` after unit heat starts at `from` (symmetric).  Async (round 70): `executor` ('cpu' | 'gpu' | 'workers' | 'auto', default 'auto') picks between per-column sparse series on the CPU, the same columns spread over the worker pool (round 74 — bit-identical to 'cpu') and the dense scaling-and-squaring chain on the GPU — under 'auto' the GPU from 256 nodes at any density (round 72.6), else the pool from 256.  `laplacian` ('combinatorial' | 'normalized', default 'combinatorial') picks L = D − A or I − D^{-½}AD^{-½} (round 72.4).  All-pairs (O(n²) memory).  v4-only — v3 has no counterpart.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.effectiveResistance
v4ApiEntries.summary: Effective resistance and commute time — the graph as a resistor network (weights are conductances): `resistance(a, b)` from the Laplacian pseudo-inverse, `commuteTime(a, b)` the expected round-trip steps of the random walk (component volume × resistance).  Pairs in different components answer Infinity. Async (round 70): `executor` ('cpu' | 'gpu' | 'auto', default 'auto') picks between dense f64 elimination on the CPU and Newton–Schulz matmul iteration on the GPU; both are O(n³), so 'auto' takes the GPU on size alone.  v4-only — v3 has no counterpart.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.motifCensus
v4ApiEntries.summary: The triad census — every three-node subgraph classified into the sixteen Holland–Leinhardt classes ('003' … '300'; '030T' is the feed-forward loop).  The counts sum to C(n, 3).  Async (round 70): `executor` ('cpu' | 'gpu' | 'auto', default 'auto'; 'workers' runs the reference on one pool worker, round 129.1) picks between sparse wedge walks on the CPU and matmul trace products on the GPU — under 'auto' the GPU only on dense graphs (a mean degree of 64, round 72.6).  `directed: false` reads every edge as mutual, so only 003 / 102 / 201 / 300 (empty / one-edge / path / triangle) can be non-zero. v4-only — v3 has no counterpart.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.kMeans
v4ApiEntries.summary: k-means clustering in attribute space.  Like v3's clustering algorithms this works on handles and `attributes` accessors rather than on graph structure.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.kMedoids
v4ApiEntries.summary: k-medoids clustering — like k-means, but cluster centres are actual elements, which makes it robust to outliers.  Async, with the same `executor` contract as `kMeans`.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.fuzzyCMeans
v4ApiEntries.summary: Fuzzy c-means clustering: each element gets a degree of membership in every cluster rather than one hard assignment.  Async, with the same `executor` contract as `kMeans`.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.hierarchicalClustering
v4ApiEntries.summary: Agglomerative hierarchical clustering.  Async (round 65): returns a promise, and `executor` ('cpu' | 'gpu' | 'auto', default 'auto'; 'workers' runs the reference on one pool worker, round 134) picks where the distance matrix is built; the merge chain itself is sequential and runs with the reference — in-thread, or on the pool worker for a named `distance` and a 'min' / 'max' / 'mean' `linkage`.  A custom `distance` function or a per-pair linkage consults the metric inside the run, on the calling thread, and 'workers' rejects them.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.markovClustering
v4ApiEntries.summary: Markov clustering (MCL) — flow simulation over the graph, so unlike the attribute-space algorithms this one clusters by structure.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.affinityPropagation
v4ApiEntries.summary: Affinity propagation, which picks exemplars by message passing and so needs no target cluster count.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.degree
v4ApiEntries.summary: The **first** element's total degree, in + out, answered in O(1) off the adjacency index.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.outdegree
v4ApiEntries.summary: The first element's out-degree, in O(1).  Singular, like `degree()`.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.indegree
v4ApiEntries.summary: The first element's in-degree, in O(1).  Singular, like `degree()`.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.minDegree
v4ApiEntries.summary: The smallest total degree among the collection's nodes.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.maxDegree
v4ApiEntries.summary: The largest total degree among the collection's nodes.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.minIndegree
v4ApiEntries.summary: The smallest in-degree among the collection's nodes.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.maxIndegree
v4ApiEntries.summary: The largest in-degree among the collection's nodes.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.minOutdegree
v4ApiEntries.summary: The smallest out-degree among the collection's nodes.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.maxOutdegree
v4ApiEntries.summary: The largest out-degree among the collection's nodes.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.totalDegree
v4ApiEntries.summary: The summed degree of every node in the collection — the whole-collection figure that `degree()` deliberately is not.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.on
v4ApiEntries.summary: Listen for events on each element of this collection.  The handler is bound per element, and keeps firing across slot compaction — listeners repair with their elements rather than going stale.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.one
v4ApiEntries.summary: Like `on()`, but each element's handler runs at most once.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.off
v4ApiEntries.summary: Stop listening on each element of this collection.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.emit
v4ApiEntries.summary: Emit an event on each element, bubbling through compound ancestors to the core.

v4ApiEntries.name: eles.promiseOn
v4ApiEntries.summary: Resolve once the next matching event fires on any element of this collection — the promise form of `one()`.

v4ApiEntries.name: ani.play
v4ApiEntries.summary: Enqueue and start.

v4ApiEntries.name: ani.stop
v4ApiEntries.summary: Stop in place, or at the targets with `jumpToEnd` — the whole animation, whatever elements it spans.  Through the manager, so a GPU-driven one releases its batch (round 144).

v4ApiEntries.name: ani.promise
v4ApiEntries.summary: The completion promise.

v4ApiEntries.name: ani.playing
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether the animation is running and not paused.

v4ApiEntries.name: ani.pause
v4ApiEntries.summary: Round 24.3: freeze in place; the paused span leaves the timeline.

v4ApiEntries.name: ani.resume
v4ApiEntries.summary: Resume a paused animation with the clock shifted (round 24.3).

v4ApiEntries.name: ani.reverse
v4ApiEntries.summary: Swap the tween's ends with elapsed remapped (round 24.3).

v4ApiEntries.name: ani.progress
v4ApiEntries.summary: Elapsed fraction of the duration (read-only — no scrubbing).

v4ApiEntries.name: ani.paused
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether the animation is paused (round 24.3).

v4ApiEntries.name: ctx.cy
v4ApiEntries.summary: the core being laid out

v4ApiEntries.name: ctx.options
v4ApiEntries.summary: the resolved layout options (custom knobs included)

v4ApiEntries.name: ctx.eles
v4ApiEntries.summary: The layout scope (handles tier); the whole graph unless this run came from `eles.layout()`.

v4ApiEntries.name: ctx.nodes
v4ApiEntries.summary: The scope's node handles (lazy — see `eles`).

v4ApiEntries.name: ctx.refreshScope
v4ApiEntries.summary: Drop the cached scope so the next `eles` / `nodes` read the graph as it now is (118.3): a whole-graph scope is materialized once per run, and a force layout's `infinite` run rebuilds its sim on an add or remove.  A subset scope (`eles.layout()`) is the caller's collection and stays what it was.

v4ApiEntries.name: ctx.nodeSlots
v4ApiEntries.summary: The slots to lay out: the scope's unlocked leaves, plus a collapsed parent when no scoped node lies below it. Locked nodes hold their place; parents with scoped descendants derive from those descendants. Scope order.

v4ApiEntries.name: ctx.edgeSlots
v4ApiEntries.summary: The scope's edge slots.

v4ApiEntries.name: ctx.positions
v4ApiEntries.summary: The live position column (x,y interleaved by slot) — read it, write through `setPositions`.

v4ApiEntries.name: ctx.endpoints
v4ApiEntries.summary: The live edge endpoint column (source,target node slots).

v4ApiEntries.name: ctx.degreeOf
v4ApiEntries.summary: O(1) degree off the CSR adjacency.

v4ApiEntries.name: ctx.nodeDimensions
v4ApiEntries.summary: The layout boxes of the scope's nodes (round 114.1): slot-parallel node-local extents read off the size, border and label columns — the one reading every built-in spaces by.  Labels are included when the run's `nodeDimensionsIncludeLabels` is `true` (115: v3's default again), making the box asymmetric when a label hangs below the body; take `max( -y1, y2 )` for a symmetric half.  Headless label dimensions are estimates (16.4), exact once a renderer has laid the glyphs.

v4ApiEntries.name: ctx.boundingBox
v4ApiEntries.summary: The scope's current bounding box, labels included.

v4ApiEntries.name: ctx.width
v4ApiEntries.summary: The viewport width in CSS px — what a layout sizing itself to the screen should use.  Headless instances report the configured headless width, so a layout still works without a DOM.

v4ApiEntries.name: ctx.height
v4ApiEntries.summary: The viewport height in CSS px.

v4ApiEntries.name: ctx.setPositions
v4ApiEntries.summary: The bulk write: xy[i*2], xy[i*2+1] land on slots[i] — one dirty span, no handles (the round-5 slot path; under compounds it takes the per-slot sequential path so auto-bounds stay exact).

v4ApiEntries.name: ctx.components
v4ApiEntries.summary: The scope's connected components over `nodeSlots()` (round 114.4, factored out of `packComponents` for layouts that pack their own arrays): union-find over the scope's own edges — an edge with an endpoint outside the scope connects nothing here — indexed by position in `nodeSlots()`.

v4ApiEntries.name: ctx.packComponents
v4ApiEntries.summary: Separate the scope's disconnected components (round 87.1): v3's `separateComponents` as a one-call, translation-only post-pass. Per-component bounding boxes at the current positions are shelf-packed largest-first with `spacing` between them, every member translated with its component, and the largest component's centre held fixed — the dominant structure keeps its place and the strays come to it.

v4ApiEntries.name: ctx.layoutPositions
v4ApiEntries.summary: The discrete finisher: v3's layoutPositions plumbing over the scope — spacingFactor, transform, animate (with the fit-at-final-positions viewport animation), fit/zoom/pan, and the layoutready/layoutstop events.  The wrapper's layoutstart covers the start (no double emit).

v4ApiEntries.name: ctx.finish
v4ApiEntries.summary: Land computed positions the way a built-in does (round 114.2): the finisher when the run asks for anything it owns — `animate`, `animateFilter`, `transform`, `spacingFactor` — and otherwise the bulk slot write followed by fit / zoom / pan.  One rule for flow, force and any extension that computes into an array.

v4ApiEntries.name: layout.options
v4ApiEntries.summary: the resolved options this run was created with

v4ApiEntries.name: layout.run
v4ApiEntries.summary: Start the layout.  Emits `layoutstart` on the core, calls `impl.run( ctx )` and awaits it if it returns a promise (the shape a GPU-resident layout needs).

v4ApiEntries.name: layout.promise
v4ApiEntries.summary: Resolves at this run's `layoutstop` (immediately when never run); rejects with `CancelledError` when the run was cancelled (round 128) — by `cancel()` or by `cy.destroy()`.

v4ApiEntries.name: layout.stop
v4ApiEntries.summary: Ask the layout to stop early, by calling the impl's optional `stop()`.  An impl without one simply runs to completion.  Once the impl has settled and only its finisher tween is in flight (round 144), the tween stops where it got to and `layoutstop` fires now, as a built-in's `stop()` does.

v4ApiEntries.name: layout.cancel
v4ApiEntries.summary: Abandon the run in flight (round 128) — the alternative to `stop()`, which keeps what stands.  The impl is asked to `cancel()` (or `stop()` when it has no `cancel`), and once its `run` settles the scope's nodes go back to where `run()` found them, a tween under way is dropped where it is, the viewport is left alone, `layoutstop` fires with `cancelled: true`, and `promise()` rejects with `CancelledError`.  A layout that is not running is unchanged.

v4ApiEntries.name: layout.reheat
v4ApiEntries.summary: Heat a running layout back up (118.3), by calling the impl's optional `reheat()`.  A force layout's `infinite` run ticks only while its field is moving and reheats itself on a drag, a moved node and an added or removed element; this is for a change it cannot see — an edge length that changed under a data mapping, a style that resized the boxes.  An impl without one ignores it.

v4ApiEntries.name: event.type
v4ApiEntries.summary: the event type, e.g. `'tap'` — never namespaced (round 41.1)

v4ApiEntries.name: event.target
v4ApiEntries.summary: the core for core-level events, the element for element events

v4ApiEntries.name: event.cy
v4ApiEntries.summary: the core the event was raised on

v4ApiEntries.name: event.position
v4ApiEntries.summary: model-space position, on pointer-derived events

v4ApiEntries.name: event.renderedPosition
v4ApiEntries.summary: rendered-space position; derived from `position` and the viewport

v4ApiEntries.name: event.originalEvent
v4ApiEntries.summary: the DOM event behind a gesture, when there was one (round 41.4)

v4ApiEntries.name: event.layout
v4ApiEntries.summary: the layout instance, on the layout lifecycle events

v4ApiEntries.name: event.cancelled
v4ApiEntries.summary: on `layoutstop`, whether the run was cancelled (round 128); on `loadstop`, whether the load was (round 103)

v4ApiEntries.name: event.diff
v4ApiEntries.summary: on `patch`, what the patch added, removed and updated (round 107)

v4ApiEntries.name: event.progress
v4ApiEntries.summary: on the load lifecycle events, the chunks and elements so far (round 103)

v4ApiEntries.name: event.timeStamp
v4ApiEntries.summary: when the event was built, `Date.now()` unless the caller supplied one

v4ApiEntries.name: event.isDefaultPrevented
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether `preventDefault()` has been called.

v4ApiEntries.name: event.isPropagationStopped
v4ApiEntries.summary: Whether `stopPropagation()` has been called — read by the compound bubbling walk (round 14.5), where it halts the phase sequence.

v4ApiEntries.name: event.preventDefault
v4ApiEntries.summary: Mark the event's default as prevented, and prevent the DOM event's default when one is attached.

v4ApiEntries.name: event.stopPropagation
v4ApiEntries.summary: Stop the event bubbling to further phases: the remaining ancestors and the core do not see it (round 14.5).  Returning `false` from a handler does the same.  With `originalEvent` attached (round 41.4) this also calls the DOM event's `stopPropagation()`, so an outer DOM listener stops seeing it too.
